source: USA Baseball American Development Model (Activate/Discover stages) + Youth Baseball Skills Matrix's Daily Practice Organization Outline + this app's own data/pitch-smart-rules.json. T-Ball and Rookies/Coach-Pitch content is adapted from Little League University's official diagrammed curricula (littleleague.org/downloads/tee-ball-program, littleleague.org/downloads/coach-pitch-12-week-program). Minors content is assembled from ADM + the Skills Matrix. Majors content has no official published curriculum anywhere (Little League's own site confirms the gap) -- those drills are sourceType 'lybs-original' and need LYBS coach review before being treated as settled.
note: Flat, atomic drill library -- a coach picks individual drills and builds their own practice, rather than adopting a pre-made weekly plan. Each drill is tagged with a 'tier' (foundational/standard/advanced) WITHIN its division: foundational is what a player new to that level needs, advanced is a stretch for players already ahead, standard is the typical mid-season expectation. Tier lives on the drill, not the team -- this app's roster has no field for a player's prior experience, so a coach judges their own team's makeup and filters to the tier(s) that fit (e.g. a team with a few new-to-Majors players and some returners might want Foundational + Standard visible together). 'category' values are drawn from data/skill-benchmarks-seed.json's own category vocabulary, plus 'Game/Scrimmage' and 'Multi-Station' for closing activities and multi-coach station rotations. Phase 1 -- migrated from the prior pre-built-practice version, not a full buildout. Phase 2 (2026) -- every drill now also carries equipment/setup/coachingPoints, and 40 of 49 drills have a diagramRef (skipped for pure warm-up/conditioning and closing-game/scrimmage drills, where a field diagram wouldn't add anything). Same sourcing discipline as Phase 1 -- this new content follows the same citation/sourceType honesty already established per drill, not new citations of its own.

drills.title: Dynamic Warm-up
drills.description: Full-body dynamic warm-up routine before throwing.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Tee Ball Program, Weeks 1-2
setup: Form two or three lines facing a coach with room to swing arms freely.
Lead the group through each movement for 20-30 seconds before switching.
Mix in arm circles, high knees, side shuffles, and torso twists.
Finish with a few standing reaches toward the sky and down to the toes.
coachingPoints: Keep movements continuous and controlled, not a race to finish.
Look for full arm circles and hip rotation, not just arm waving.
Use this time to get names and energy up before equipment comes out.

drills.title: Partner Throw & Catch
drills.description: Partner throw and catch at soft-toss distance.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Tee Ball Program, Weeks 1-2
setup: Pair players up by similar size and arm strength where possible.
Space each pair about 10-15 feet apart, facing one another.
One partner throws overhand, the other catches with two hands.
Switch roles every 5-6 throws so both partners throw and catch.
Walk the lines and reset spacing or pairs as needed.
coachingPoints: Check for a proper 4-seam grip before each throw.
Remind catchers to use two hands and watch the ball all the way in.
Encourage an overhand motion, not sidearm or underhand.

drills.title: Tee Hitting, One Station
drills.description: Tee hitting, single station -- group rotates through.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Tee Ball Program, Weeks 1-2
setup: Set up one or more tees at the front of the hitting area.
Line the group up single file behind the hitter.
Each hitter takes 5-6 swings, then rotates to the back of the line.
Have a helper reset the ball on the tee and shag balls between hitters.
coachingPoints: Check for a balanced, athletic stance before each swing.
Watch that the swing stays level, not a big uppercut or chop.
Set the ball at the hitter's belly-button height on the tee.

drills.title: 3-Station Rotation: Throw/Catch, Tee, Fielding
drills.description: Split the group into three stations and rotate every ~10 minutes. Needs about 3 coaches/helpers to run all stations at once.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Tee Ball Program, Weeks 1-2
setup: Set up three stations: throw & catch, tee hitting, and rolled-ball fielding.
Split the group into three even groups, one per station.
Station a coach or helper at each station to run the activity.
Rotate groups to the next station every ~10 minutes on a call or whistle.
Keep the same rep structure at each station so rotations stay predictable.
coachingPoints: At throw & catch: look for a 4-seam grip and two-handed catches.
At the tee: check stance balance and a level swing path.
At fielding: make sure players get in front of the ball with two hands.
Keep transitions quick so stations don't lose momentum.

drills.title: Soft Toss Introduction
drills.description: Soft toss (a moving ball, not a tee) -- a stretch into Rookies-level hitting for kids already catching/hitting consistently.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Tee Ball Program, Weeks 1-2
setup: Have the tosser kneel or stand to the side, slightly in front of the hitter.
Toss the ball underhand on a soft, flat arc into the hitting zone.
Each hitter takes 5-6 swings, then rotates.
Start with a slower, predictable toss and speed up as timing improves.
coachingPoints: Watch for the hitter tracking the moving ball, not swinging early.
Keep the swing path level, same as tee work.
Toss to the same spot each time so timing is the only variable.

drills.title: Two-Handed Catch Reps, Close Distance
drills.description: Extra reps for kids still building basic catch comfort -- shorten the toss distance and emphasize two hands.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Tee Ball Program, Weeks 1-2
setup: Pair players up, standing 5-8 feet apart.
Toss the ball gently and directly at the catcher's chest.
Catcher uses two hands and brings the ball in to their body.
Take turns tossing and catching, 8-10 reps each.
Shorten the distance further for any player still struggling.
coachingPoints: Two hands together -- bare hand covers the glove on the catch.
Eyes on the ball all the way into the glove.
Keep tosses soft, chest-high, and predictable to build confidence.

drills.title: Tee Stance & Swing-Path Reps
drills.description: Extra reps on tee stance and swing path for kids still building comfort at the tee.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Tee Ball Program, Weeks 1-2
setup: Set the tee at the hitter's belly-button height.
Start with dry swings, no ball, to check stance and setup.
Add a ball and take 5-6 swings focusing on stance and path, not power.
Rotate hitters through in small groups for individual feedback.
coachingPoints: Feet shoulder-width apart, weight balanced, not leaning back.
Hands start from the same comfortable spot every swing.
Swing finishes through contact instead of stopping at the ball.

drills.title: Run-Through-First Reps
drills.description: Run-through-first-base reps, no admiring the hit.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Tee Ball Program, base-running activities
setup: Line players up at home plate single file.
Each player runs hard through first base without slowing to look.
A coach at first base calls safe/out or simply cues the finish.
Rotate the next runner once the base is clear.
Repeat for 2-3 full sets.
coachingPoints: Run through the bag at full speed -- no peeking at the ball.
Step on the front of the base, not the middle, and don't jump at it.
Run in a straight line to first, not drifting into foul territory.

drills.title: 2-Station Rotation: Base Running, Throw/Catch
drills.description: Split into two stations and rotate -- base running on one side, throw & catch pairs on the other.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Tee Ball Program, base-running activities
setup: Split the group into two even groups, one per station.
Run run-through-first reps on one side, throw & catch pairs on the other.
Rotate groups halfway through the allotted time.
Keep each station simple enough for one helper to run.
coachingPoints: Base-running side: full speed through the bag, no slowing early.
Throwing side: 4-seam grip and two-handed catches.
Keep both stations running at once so no one stands around.

drills.title: Secondary Lead Introduction
drills.description: Secondary lead off a base -- a stretch into Rookies-level base running.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Tee Ball Program, base-running activities
setup: Start players standing on a base with a coach at the pitching spot.
Runner takes a few shuffle steps off the base as the pitch is released.
Freeze the lead and check balance before continuing.
Runner retreats back to the base safely between reps.
Rotate through 4-5 runners at a time.
coachingPoints: Lead with shuffle steps, not a big crossover, to stay balanced.
Stay low and ready to retreat quickly.
Watch the pitcher while taking the lead, not the ground.

drills.title: Run-Through-First Reps, Extra Sets
drills.description: Extra sets of run-through-first reps for kids still building the habit.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Tee Ball Program, base-running activities
setup: Line players up at home plate single file, keeping the line short for more reps.
Each player runs through first base at full speed.
Give brief individual feedback after each rep before the next runner goes.
Run extra sets (4-5 total) for players still building the habit.
coachingPoints: Full speed through the bag on every rep, no exceptions.
Step on the front of the base, running through rather than to it.
Praise the habit of running hard even on a routine play.

drills.title: Closing Game
drills.description: A fun closing game or mini scrimmage to wrap up practice.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Tee Ball Program
setup: Split the group into two teams for a mini scrimmage or closing game.
Use simplified rules (everyone bats, no strikeouts) to keep it fast and fun.
Rotate positions each inning or after every batter so everyone fields and hits.
Keep score light -- the focus is fun, not competition.
coachingPoints: Use the game to reinforce the day's focus (e.g. running through first).
Keep energy high and celebrate effort, not just outcomes.
End on a positive note, win or lose.

drills.title: Dynamic Warm-up
drills.description: Full-body dynamic warm-up routine before throwing.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Coach Pitch 12-Week Program, Weeks 1-2
equipment: Cones (to mark start and finish lines)
Open grass area or outfield space
setup: Gather the full team in a line along the foul line or outfield grass, spaced an arm's length apart.
Lead the group through each movement for 20-30 feet down and back: jogging, high knees, butt kicks, lateral shuffles, arm circles.
Finish with dynamic stretches for hips, hamstrings, and shoulders (walking lunges, leg swings).
Cycle through 2 full sets before moving into throwing.
coachingPoints: Watch for kids rushing through movements without full range of motion.
Keep the pace brisk so bodies warm up -- it's not a race.
Save any held/static stretching for after practice, not before throwing.

drills.title: Crow-Hop Throwing Reps
drills.description: Crow-hop throw with intent, building power into the throw.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Coach Pitch 12-Week Program, Weeks 1-2
setup: Pair players up facing each other, 20-30 feet apart along a foul line or open grass area.
Demonstrate the crow-hop footwork: catch, pivot on the back foot, small hop/step toward the target, then throw.
Have each pair work through sets of 8-10 throws, alternating who throws and who catches.
Gradually increase the distance between partners as accuracy and arm strength allow.
Rotate partners halfway through so players throw to a few different targets.
coachingPoints: Hop should be a quick shuffle toward the target, not a big jump that kills momentum.
Throwing arm finishes low and across the body -- no stopping at release.
Front shoulder points at the target through the whole throw.

diagramRef.title: Crow-hop throwing lane
diagramRef.note: Run along open outfield grass for space

drills.title: Rolled Grounders, Two Hands
drills.description: Field a rolled or slow-bounced grounder with two hands.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Coach Pitch 12-Week Program, Weeks 1-2
setup: Line players up single-file at an infield spot, gloves down and ready in a fielding position.
Coach rolls a ball firmly along the ground to each player in turn.
Fielder shuffles in front of the ball and fields it with two hands, staying low.
After fielding, player makes a short throw back to the coach or a target, then jogs to the back of the line.
Repeat for several rounds, varying the roll slightly left and right of the fielder.
coachingPoints: Glove goes down early and stays open toward the ball -- no last-second stabs.
Both hands come together on the ball before the throwing hand transfers it.
Feet move to get the body in front of the ball rather than reaching to the side.

drills.title: 3-Station Rotation: Throwing, Grounders, Ready Position
drills.description: Split the group into three stations and rotate every ~10 minutes.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Coach Pitch 12-Week Program, Weeks 1-2
setup: Split the team into three equal groups, one per station.
Station 1 (Throwing): partners run crow-hop throwing reps at a safe distance apart.
Station 2 (Grounders): coach or helper rolls grounders for two-handed fielding reps.
Station 3 (Ready Position): players practice getting into an athletic ready position on a coach's "pitch" cue, no ball needed.
Rotate all three groups every ~10 minutes on a whistle or call.
Use a parent helper or assistant coach at each station if available.
coachingPoints: Keep reps high and lines moving -- no station should have kids standing around.
Apply the same cues as the standalone drills at each station (soft hands, two-hand transfer, shuffle to the ball).
Use a consistent rotation signal so kids know when to switch without confusion.

drills.title: Live-Speed Grounders
drills.description: A stretch into Minors-level fielding speed -- hit or throw grounders at game speed instead of rolled.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Coach Pitch 12-Week Program, Weeks 1-2
equipment: Bat (if hitting grounders instead of rolling them)
setup: Line players up at normal infield positions (shortstop/third base area) rather than close in.
Coach hits or throws grounders at a quicker, game-like pace instead of rolling them.
Fielder gets in front of the ball, fields with two hands, and makes a throw to a target.
Rotate through the line, giving each player several reps before adjusting speed or placement.
Mix in a few balls hit slightly to either side to start building lateral range.
coachingPoints: This is a stretch drill -- ease off the speed for any player who looks rushed or hesitant.
Same fundamentals as rolled grounders apply: glove down early, two hands, shuffle rather than reach.
Look for a quick, compact transfer to throw since there's less reaction time than a rolled ball.

diagramRef.title: Live-speed grounders spot
diagramRef.note: Positioned deeper/truer to infield depth than the rolled-grounder drills

drills.title: Catching Off-Glove-Side Reps
drills.description: Extra reps catching a ball thrown slightly off to the glove side.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Coach Pitch 12-Week Program, Weeks 1-2
equipment: Soft or reduced-impact balls (for less confident catchers)
setup: Pair players up facing each other, 10-15 feet apart.
One partner tosses the ball slightly to the glove side of the catcher, not directly at the chest.
Catcher works on moving the feet and glove to get square to the ball before catching.
Run sets of 8-10 tosses, then switch roles.
Gradually widen the angle of the toss as players get comfortable reaching to that side.
coachingPoints: Feet move first -- don't let players stay flat-footed and just reach with the glove.
Glove fingers point up/out toward the ball on the glove side, not down.
Keep tosses soft and catchable early; only speed up once the footwork looks right.

drills.title: Rolled Grounder Reps, Closer Distance
drills.description: Rolled grounder reps at a closer distance for kids still building comfort.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Coach Pitch 12-Week Program, Weeks 1-2
setup: Set up the same as the standard rolled-grounder drill, but move the line in to a shorter distance from the coach.
Roll the ball gently and directly at each player so they can focus on the catch, not the approach.
Each player fields with two hands, then flips or tosses the ball back underhand.
Give these players extra reps/rounds before matching the standard distance.
Slowly increase the distance back toward the standard spot as confidence builds.
coachingPoints: Success here is about building confidence -- keep rolls soft and predictable.
Still demand two hands and an early glove-down, even at the closer distance.
Praise good fielding position even on a missed catch; the habit matters more than the result right now.

diagramRef.title: Close-distance grounders
diagramRef.note: Closer to home plate than the standard rolled-grounder station

drills.title: Soft Toss Hitting
drills.description: Soft toss hitting, balanced swing.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Coach Pitch 12-Week Program, Weeks 5-6
setup: Set up a net or screen with the batter standing in front, feeder kneeling to the side at a 45-degree angle.
Feeder tosses the ball underhand into the same spot in the hitting zone each time.
Batter takes a balanced swing, focusing on a level path through the ball.
Run sets of 8-10 swings per batter, then rotate the next player in.
Have waiting players shag balls or work on a tee off to the side.
coachingPoints: Front foot stays short and quiet -- no big lunging stride at the toss.
Eyes track the ball all the way into contact.
Swing stays level and balanced through the zone; watch that the finish isn't off-balance.

drills.title: Mound Mechanics Introduction
drills.description: Basic mound mechanics introduction, fastball only.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Coach Pitch 12-Week Program, Weeks 5-6
setup: Walk each pitcher through the basic setup on the rubber: pivot foot, grip, and starting position.
Break the delivery into parts -- rock/step back, knee lift, stride toward the target, release, follow-through.
Have pitchers walk through the motion slowly a few times before adding speed.
Progress to throwing fastballs only, into a catcher or screen, in short sets of 5-6 pitches.
Rotate pitchers through so everyone gets mound reps.
coachingPoints: Stride lands toward the target, not across the body or wide open.
Front side (shoulder/hip) stays closed until landing, then rotates through.
Focus on fastball command only -- no breaking pitches at this stage.

drills.title: 3-Station Rotation: Soft Toss, Mound Mechanics, Positioning
drills.description: Split the group into three stations and rotate every ~10 minutes.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Coach Pitch 12-Week Program, Weeks 5-6
setup: Split the team into three groups, one per station.
Station 1 (Soft Toss): hitters work through soft toss swings as in the standalone drill.
Station 2 (Mound Mechanics): pitchers work mound setup and delivery mechanics.
Station 3 (Positioning): coach walks players through where to stand and where to back up on a batted ball.
Rotate groups every ~10 minutes on a coach's signal.
coachingPoints: Keep an adult at each station so no group is unsupervised with a bat or ball.
Reinforce the same cues used in the individual drills at each station.
Use consistent rotation timing so transitions don't eat into practice time.

drills.title: Front Toss, Timing a Moving Ball
drills.description: A stretch into Minors-level timing -- front toss / coach pitch instead of soft toss.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Coach Pitch 12-Week Program, Weeks 5-6
setup: Set up a protective screen roughly halfway between the mound and home plate.
Coach tosses the ball from behind the screen with an easy, consistent motion toward the strike zone.
Batter times the load and stride to the moving ball rather than reacting to a stationary toss.
Run short sets of 5-6 pitches per batter, giving feedback between rounds.
Mix in a few pitches to different parts of the zone once timing looks solid.
coachingPoints: Load and stride should start as the ball leaves the coach's hand, not after.
Watch for a quiet front foot -- a stride that starts too early means the timing is off.
This is a stretch drill, so prioritize good swings over solid contact at first.

diagramRef.title: Front toss station
diagramRef.note: Screen set up closer to the plate than a full mound distance

drills.title: Soft Toss Reps, Extra Sets
drills.description: Extra sets of soft toss reps for kids still building timing.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Coach Pitch 12-Week Program, Weeks 5-6
setup: Set up a second soft-toss station away from the main group so these players get extra, unhurried reps.
Feeder kneels at a 45-degree angle and tosses underhand into the same spot each time.
Batter takes a balanced swing, focusing on seeing the ball and making contact before worrying about power.
Run extra sets (12-15 swings) per player compared to the standard drill.
Keep tosses slow and consistent until timing and balance both look comfortable.
coachingPoints: Prioritize consistent contact and balance over bat speed at this stage.
Keep the toss landing in the same spot every time so the hitter can groove the swing.
Give short, encouraging feedback between swings -- this group needs reps and confidence, not a long list of corrections.

diagramRef.title: Extra soft toss station
diagramRef.note: A second station run apart from the main soft-toss group

drills.title: Fun At Bat Game
drills.description: Fun At Bat modified-game format to close out practice.
drills.citation: Adapted from Little League University's Coach Pitch 12-Week Program
setup: Set up a modified game format (e.g., every player bats each inning, no strikeouts, coach pitch).
Divide the team into two squads if numbers allow, or play with one team batting and one fielding.
Rotate fielding positions each inning so every player gets different reps.
Apply simplified rules appropriate for the group's skill level (e.g., no leading off, modified base-running).
Keep the format loose and encouraging to end practice on a fun, game-like note.
coachingPoints: Keep it upbeat -- this is meant to feel like a reward, not another drill.
Use the live reps to reinforce what was covered earlier in practice (contact, fielding position, hustling to first).
Give quick, positive in-the-moment feedback rather than stopping play to coach extensively.

drills.title: Dynamic Warm-up
drills.description: Full-body dynamic warm-up routine before throwing.
drills.citation: USA Baseball ADM Discover stage + Skills Matrix Daily Practice Organization Outline, 10-12 band
setup: Line players up in two even rows at one end of the outfield grass.
Lead the group through each movement down and back to a cone 30-40 ft away: jogging, high knees, butt kicks, lateral shuffles, walking lunges.
Finish with arm circles and a few dynamic stretches before moving into partner throwing.
Keep the pace brisk so the whole sequence fits inside about 10 minutes.
coachingPoints: Full range of motion on each movement, not just going through it
Watch for rounded backs on lunges or crossed feet on shuffles
Use this time to spot anyone moving stiffly before throwing starts

drills.title: Accuracy Throwing to a Target
drills.description: Throw accurately to a chest-high target from infield distance.
drills.citation: USA Baseball ADM Discover stage + Skills Matrix Daily Practice Organization Outline, 10-12 band
setup: Pair players up and space each pair about 45-60 ft apart, standard infield throwing distance.
Receiving partner sets a stationary glove target at chest height and holds still.
Throwers work in sets of 8-10 throws, aiming for the glove without making the receiver move.
Switch roles after each set so both partners throw and receive.
Move pairs farther apart as accuracy holds up.
coachingPoints: Target the glove itself, not just the general area
Step toward the target with the glove-side foot on release
Full follow-through, arm finishing down and across the body

drills.title: Front Toss, Single Station
drills.description: Front toss / coach pitch, single station -- group rotates through.
drills.citation: USA Baseball ADM Discover stage + Skills Matrix Daily Practice Organization Outline, 10-12 band
setup: Set the L-screen about 10-12 ft in front of and to the side of home plate for coach protection.
Batter sets up at the plate while the coach kneels behind the screen and tosses underhand on a flat, chest-high arc.
Each hitter takes a set of 8-10 swings before rotating out.
Players not hitting shag balls and stage the next hitter so the line keeps moving.
Call the next hitter up before the current one finishes collecting their bat and helmet.
coachingPoints: Keep the toss consistent in speed and location so the hitter is timing a pitch, not reacting to randomness
Load/stride should start as the ball leaves the coach's hand, not after
Watch for hitters bailing out instead of staying balanced through contact

drills.title: 3-Station Rotation: Throwing, Infield, Front Toss
drills.description: Split the group into three stations and rotate every ~10 minutes.
drills.citation: USA Baseball ADM Discover stage + Skills Matrix Daily Practice Organization Outline, 10-12 band
setup: Split the full group into three even stations: throwing pairs, infield grounders, and front toss.
Assign a coach or helper to run each station so reps don't stall.
Stage equipment (bucket of balls, L-screen) at each station ahead of time.
Run each station for about 10 minutes, then call the rotation.
Rotate every group to the next station in the same order each time.
coachingPoints: Keep all three stations moving at once -- one stalled station wastes the whole group's time
At the infield station, check for two hands and squaring up before the throw
At front toss, keep the hitting line moving so everyone gets full reps in their window

drills.title: Live BP Introduction, 2-Strike Approach
drills.description: Live batting practice introduction, including a 2-strike approach -- for players ready to move past front toss.
drills.citation: USA Baseball ADM Discover stage + Skills Matrix Daily Practice Organization Outline, 10-12 band
setup: Set a coach or machine pitching from the mound (or slightly in front) behind the L-screen.
Hitters go in a set batting order, each taking a full at-bat (6-8 pitches).
Call balls and strikes out loud for every pitch so hitters play from a real count.
Once a hitter reaches two strikes, call it and have them shift to a shorter, protect-the-plate swing for the rest of that at-bat.
Log the at-bat on the Pitch Chart, then bring the next hitter in right away.
coachingPoints: Look for a visibly shorter load and swing once the count reaches two strikes
Reinforce taking close pitches early in the count instead of expanding the zone
Use the Pitch Chart afterward to show each hitter their own patterns

drills.title: Soft Toss & Tee Work
drills.description: Back to soft toss and tee work for players not yet front-toss consistent.
drills.citation: USA Baseball ADM Discover stage + Skills Matrix Daily Practice Organization Outline, 10-12 band
setup: Set up two stations side by side: a tee facing a net, and a soft-toss station with a tosser kneeling at a 45-degree angle in front of the net.
Split the group evenly between the two stations.
Tee hitters take sets of 8-10 swings, resetting the ball after every hit.
Soft-toss hitters take sets of 8-10 from a tosser kneeling low and to the side.
Swap the two groups halfway through so everyone gets both kinds of reps.
coachingPoints: At the tee, the swing should stay level and finish through contact rather than chop down
At soft toss, the tosser stays low and to the side so the ball doesn't drift toward the hitter's body
Check for consistent back-to-front weight transfer on every rep at both stations

drills.title: Fly Ball Reads & Tag-Up Calls
drills.description: Track and catch a fly ball hit in the air; read whether to tag up or advance.
drills.citation: USA Baseball ADM Discover stage + Skills Matrix Team Situational category, 10-12 band
setup: Station outfielders in the outfield grass; coach hits or throws fly balls from the infield.
Put a runner on 2nd or 3rd for each rep so the outfielder has to make a real read call.
On every fly ball, the outfielder calls 'tag up' or 'go' loud enough for the runner to hear before the catch.
Rotate runners and outfielders so everyone gets reps both catching and reading as a baserunner.
Mix in some balls with no runner so players also just track and catch clean.
coachingPoints: Call must come before the catch, not after -- it's a base-running cue as much as a catching one
Check that the runner tags up correctly (foot on the bag) when 'tag up' is called
Glove should come up early to track the ball, not at the last second

diagramRef.title: Fly ball reads & tag-up
diagramRef.note: Mix in reps with no runner too

drills.title: Cutoff & Relay Introduction
drills.description: Understands cutoff and relay positioning.
drills.citation: USA Baseball ADM Discover stage + Skills Matrix Team Situational category, 10-12 band
setup: Position an outfielder in left or right field, a cutoff infielder in short-center relay alignment, and a target at home.
Coach hits or throws a ball into the outfield gap.
Outfielder fields it and hits the cutoff man; cutoff turns and relays to the target.
Rotate players through outfield, cutoff, and target roles every few reps.
Start with no base runners so players can focus on the mechanics, then add a runner once the pattern is clean.
coachingPoints: Cutoff player shuffles into line with the throw and calls 'Cut!' or 'Let it go!' based on the play
Catch with two hands and turn to throw in one motion, not catch-stop-throw
Outfielder's throw should be low and on a line to the cutoff man's chest, not a lob

diagramRef.title: Cutoff & relay alignment
diagramRef.note: Add a runner once mechanics are clean

drills.title: 3-Station Rotation: Fly Balls, Grounders, Catcher Basics
drills.description: Split the group into three stations and rotate every ~10 minutes.
drills.citation: USA Baseball ADM Discover stage + Skills Matrix Team Situational category, 10-12 band
setup: Split the group into three even stations: fly ball reads, infield grounders, and catcher stance/target.
Assign a coach or helper to each station so reps keep moving.
Run each station for about 10 minutes before rotating.
At the catcher station, put every player through a few reps in gear, not just catchers.
Call rotations clearly so all three groups move together.
coachingPoints: At the fly ball station, check for an early glove-up tracking position, not a last-second stab
At the grounder station, emphasize two hands and squaring up before the throw
At the catcher station, watch for a low, steady stance and a target that doesn't drift

drills.title: Backhand Fielding Reps
drills.description: A stretch into Majors-level fielding range -- backhand a grounder hit to the glove side.
drills.citation: USA Baseball ADM Discover stage + Skills Matrix Team Situational category, 10-12 band
setup: Position players at shortstop or third-base depth; coach hits or rolls balls to the glove side.
Start with rolled or soft-hit balls angled so the player has to backhand rather than shuffle in front.
Fielder turns the glove over, plants the back foot, and throws.
Progress from rolled balls to live-speed grounders as the backhand gets cleaner.
Work in small groups of 3-4 so reps come quickly.
coachingPoints: Glove should turn fully over (fingers down), not stay upright trying to scoop it
Back-foot plant and a quick-set throw -- a backhand often can't use a full, routine set
Don't let players round the ball to field it like a forehand play

drills.title: Rolled Grounder Reps, Two Hands
drills.description: Back-to-basics rolled grounder reps for players still building clean fundamentals.
drills.citation: USA Baseball ADM Discover stage + Skills Matrix Team Situational category, 10-12 band
setup: Line up players in small groups of 3-4 at infield positions.
Coach or partner rolls (not hits) the ball directly at the fielder from short distance.
Fielder gets into the ready position and moves the feet to get in front of the ball.
Fielder fields with two hands, squares up, and throws to a target every rep.
Increase rep speed only once clean two-hand fielding is consistent.
coachingPoints: Two hands on every rep -- glove down and out front, bare hand ready to cover
Feet move to get the body in front of the ball instead of reaching off to the side
Feet reset and step toward the target on the throw, not throwing off the back foot

drills.title: Scrimmage
drills.description: Live scrimmage, folding in cutoff/relay reps where they come up.
drills.citation: USA Baseball ADM Discover stage + Skills Matrix Daily Practice Organization Outline
setup: Split into two teams, or use the full roster against coach-pitch innings if numbers are short.
Play live using regular game rules and defensive positioning.
Pause briefly to coach through a cutoff/relay or situational play right after it happens.
Rotate positions between innings so players see different spots on the field.
Use pitch counts or inning limits so everyone gets game at-bats.
coachingPoints: Let plays develop; coach situational decisions right after they happen, while it's fresh
Watch for correct backup positioning and communication calls ('I got it') during live action
Use this as an evaluation window for who's ready to move up a tier on specific skills

drills.title: Dynamic Warm-up
drills.description: Full-body dynamic warm-up routine before throwing.
drills.citation: Adapted from ADM Discover/Progress stage guidance -- no official Majors curriculum exists anywhere; review before treating as settled.
setup: Line players up in two rows facing each other, about 15-20 yards apart.
Lead the group down and back through each movement: high knees, butt kicks, walking lunges, lateral shuffles, arm circles.
Finish with light jogging and controlled arm swings to raise heart rate before throwing.
Move straight into partner catch-play once the group is loose.
coachingPoints: Full range of motion on lunges and leg swings, not shortened reps.
Controlled pace down and back, not a race to the other line.
Arms loose and shoulders warm before anyone throws at full speed.

drills.title: Live BP
drills.description: Full live batting practice off a coach or pitching-machine arm; track pitch counts/calls on the Pitch Chart tool while it runs.
drills.citation: Adapted from ADM Discover/Progress stage guidance + this app's own data/pitch-smart-rules.json -- no official Majors curriculum exists anywhere; review before treating as settled.
setup: Set the pitcher (coach or machine) behind an L-screen at full mound distance.
Hitters rotate through in a set order, one at-bat or set pitch count each.
Log every pitch's call and count on the Pitch Chart tool as it runs.
Mix locations and counts to simulate real at-bats, including 2-strike counts.
Keep on-deck and in-the-hole hitters moving so the line doesn't stall.
coachingPoints: Hitters shorten up and protect the plate once they're down to their last strike.
Watch for a consistent load and stride against full-speed pitching, not rushing the swing.
Pitch Chart stays current in real time — that's the point of running this live.

diagramRef.title: Live BP setup
diagramRef.note: Coach/machine at mound distance throwing to the batter.

drills.title: Pitch Count & Rest-Day Rules Walkthrough
drills.description: Walk the team through their own pitch count and the rest-day rules that follow -- this app's own Pitch Smart data.
drills.citation: This app's own data/pitch-smart-rules.json, sourced from MAC League's Pitch Smart tables
setup: Gather the team and pull up each pitcher's current pitch count from the app's Pitch Smart data.
Walk through which count range triggers which rest-day requirement.
Have each pitcher state their own current count and the rest days it requires.
Cover the mid-batter exception: a pitcher who hits the max can finish that batter before coming out.
coachingPoints: Every pitcher can state their own count and rest requirement without being prompted.
No ambiguity left about the mid-batter exception — it's the rule players mix up most.

drills.title: Station Rotation: Live BP, Relay Throws, Catcher Blocking
drills.description: Split the group into three stations and rotate.
drills.citation: Adapted from ADM Discover/Progress stage guidance -- no official Majors curriculum exists anywhere; review before treating as settled.
setup: Split the group evenly across three stations: Live BP, Relay Throws, Catcher Blocking.
Run each station for a set time (8-12 minutes) with a coach leading it.
Rotate all groups to the next station on a whistle or call.
Live BP station follows standard live-pitching rules with Pitch Chart tracking.
Relay station works outfield-to-relay-to-base throws; Catcher Blocking works balls in the dirt.
coachingPoints: Each station coach keeps reps high — don't let players stand around waiting for a turn.
Relay throws emphasize a quick catch-and-release, not just catching the ball cleanly.
Catchers stay square to the ball and smother it rather than stab at it with the glove.

drills.title: Situational Hitting -- Move the Runner Over
drills.description: Situational hitting for experienced Majors hitters -- move the runner over, hit behind the runner.
drills.citation: Adapted from ADM Progress stage team-play guidance -- no official Majors curriculum exists anywhere; review before treating as settled.
setup: Put a runner on 2nd base (live or simulated) with a hitter at the plate.
Coach pitches or soft-tosses at a live-ish speed to the hitter.
Hitter's job each rep is to move the runner to 3rd — ground ball to the right side or a deep fly.
Rotate hitters through in a line, giving each several reps before switching roles.
coachingPoints: Hitter adjusts to the situation — a pulled ground ball to the right side counts as success even if it's an out.
Watch for hitters trying to pull and lift the ball instead of staying through it the other way.

drills.title: Front Toss Timing Reps
drills.description: For players new to Majors-level pitching speed -- back to front toss timing before live BP.
drills.citation: Adapted from ADM Discover/Progress stage guidance -- no official Majors curriculum exists anywhere; review before treating as settled.
setup: Coach kneels or stands roughly 15-20 feet in front of the plate, behind a screen if available.
Toss underhand at a moderate, consistent speed so timing is the focus, not velocity.
Hitter takes 8-10 swings before rotating out for the next player.
Gradually increase toss speed as the hitter's timing holds up.
Move hitters to live BP once their timing is consistent at this speed.
coachingPoints: Front foot lands before the swing starts — timing the stride is the whole point of this drill.
No rushing or lunging at the ball just because it's slower than live pitching.

drills.title: Relay Throw Reps
drills.description: Relay throw mechanics -- hit the cutoff man.
drills.citation: Adapted from ADM Progress stage team-play guidance -- no official Majors curriculum exists anywhere; review before treating as settled.
setup: Place an outfielder in left or right field, a relay man in shallow outfield/infield, and a target at home or a base.
Coach hits or throws a ball out to the outfielder.
Outfielder fields it and hits the relay man with a low, catchable throw.
Relay man pivots and fires to the target without an extra hitch.
Rotate players through all three roles.
coachingPoints: Relay man gets his glove-side foot toward the target before the ball even arrives.
First throw only needs to reach the relay man on time, not the final target.
Watch for a quick catch-and-release at the relay spot, not a double-clutch.

drills.title: Bunt Defense Walkthrough
drills.description: Execute bunt-defense assignments as a team.
drills.citation: Adapted from ADM Progress stage team-play guidance -- no official Majors curriculum exists anywhere; review before treating as settled.
setup: Walk the defense through each assignment with no ball first: pitcher covers the middle, corners charge.
Assign who covers 1st and 3rd on the throw once a corner infielder charges the bunt.
Add a bunter and run it live at half speed so fielders find their landmarks.
Increase to full speed once assignments are clean.
Repeat with runners on different bases to cover each bunt-defense look the team will see.
coachingPoints: Whoever charges the bunt calls it loudly so nobody else goes for the same ball.
Covering fielders are already moving to the bag before the throw, not waiting on it.
Pitcher breaks off the mound toward the bunt side, not standing flat-footed.

drills.title: Station Rotation: Relays, Double Plays, Rundowns
drills.description: Split the group into three stations and rotate.
drills.citation: Adapted from ADM Progress stage team-play guidance -- no official Majors curriculum exists anywhere; review before treating as settled.
setup: Split the group evenly across three stations: Relay Throws, Double Plays, Rundowns.
Run each station for a set time (8-12 minutes) with a coach leading it.
Rotate all groups to the next station on a whistle or call.
Double-play station works the feed and pivot at 2nd from both the shortstop and second-base side.
Rundown station works a runner caught between bases with two defenders.
coachingPoints: Double-play pivot foot finds the bag before the ball arrives, not after.
Rundown defenders throw only when the runner commits, not on every catch.
Relay throws stay low and on a line, not lobbed.

drills.title: Stolen-Base Read Reps
drills.description: Read a pitcher's move and time a stolen-base jump -- for experienced Majors base runners.
drills.citation: Adapted from ADM Progress stage guidance -- no official Majors curriculum exists anywhere; review before treating as settled.
setup: Put a runner on 1st (or 2nd) with a coach or pitcher on the mound mixing pickoffs and deliveries.
Runner takes a secondary lead and reads the pitcher's first move each rep.
Time the runner's jump and sprint to the next base with the Base Running timer.
Mix in real pickoff throws so the runner has to react for real, not just guess.
Rotate runners through so everyone gets multiple reads.
coachingPoints: Runner reacts to the pitcher's first move, not to the ball leaving the hand.
Watch for a runner guessing and leaving early — that's a pickoff waiting to happen, not a good jump.

drills.title: Live-Speed Grounder & Throw Reps
drills.description: For players new to Majors-level grounder speed -- live-speed grounders with a throw to first.
drills.citation: Adapted from ADM Discover/Progress stage guidance -- no official Majors curriculum exists anywhere; review before treating as settled.
setup: Position fielders at short or third with a first baseman set up to receive.
Coach hits or throws live-speed ground balls to each fielder in turn.
Fielder fields it cleanly, sets their feet, and throws across to 1st.
Rotate through all infield spots so everyone gets reps at live speed.
Start straight-on, then add balls to each side once the basic rep is clean.
coachingPoints: Glove down early and through the ball, not stabbing at the last second.
Feet set and throw on balance — a rushed, off-balance throw is worse than a slightly late one.

drills.title: Scrimmage
drills.description: Live scrimmage to close out practice.
drills.citation: Adapted from ADM Discover/Progress stage guidance -- no official Majors curriculum exists anywhere; review before treating as settled.
setup: Split into two teams, or use both dugouts if it's a combined practice.
Play a live scrimmage under normal game rules to close out practice.
Rotate positions and at-bats so everyone gets meaningful playing time.
Use it to reinforce whatever the day's practice focused on at live game speed.
coachingPoints: Let plays develop — this is the time to apply what was drilled, not to over-coach every pitch.
Flag situational mistakes briefly between innings rather than stopping play mid-at-bat.
